item.title: Inline Brand Cues Should Support the Copy, Not Fight the Headline
item.description: Subtle inline brand emphasis can make important names and concepts easier to scan, but only when it supports the page hierarchy instead of competing with it.

item.title: Page Images Need a System, Not a Search Spree
item.description: Website images should be chosen, mapped, and maintained like content. A simple image system keeps pages from feeling generic, repetitive, or disconnected.

item.title: Claim Hygiene Is Part of Website QA
item.description: High-trust websites need more than polished design. Every public claim should be defensible, crawlable, and aligned with the facts the site can prove.

item.title: Customer-Facing Pages Should Not Show the Strategy
item.description: A website can be built for SEO, AI search, conversion, and authority without telling visitors about the strategy. Buyers need answers, not behind-the-scenes labels.

item.title: The Website Rebuild Step That Saves the Whole Project
item.description: Before rebuilding a business website, inventory the current pages, images, content, and conversion paths. It prevents redesigns from losing useful assets and search value.

item.title: When Local Businesses Outgrow Manual Marketing
item.description: A local business can build real attention through social media and still struggle to keep marketing consistent. The solution is not more hustle. It is a better system.

item.title: Why Local Service Businesses Score Well on Technical SEO but Fail AI Citability
item.description: Local service businesses often have solid technical SEO — HTTPS, schema, sitemap, fast load times. But when it comes to AI citability, they're invisible. Here's the structural reason why.

item.title: What a 4-Dimensional AI Visibility Audit Actually Looks Like
item.description: Most GEO audits are a checklist. A real audit measures four distinct dimensions — and which one is weakest tells you more about a site than the total score does.
